metadata.note: The Atchison and Nebraska Railroad (consolidated 10 Aug 1871 from the Atchison & Nebraska Rail Road of Kansas and the Atchison, Lincoln & Columbus of Nebraska) built one main line and no branches: Atchison KS - White Cloud - Rulo - Falls City - Humboldt - Table Rock - Tecumseh - Lincoln NE (144.91 mi to Lancaster; ~148 mi to Lincoln over ~4 mi of Nebraska Railway trackage). It ran its own trains 1871/72 - 31 Dec 1879; leased 999 years to the Burlington & Missouri River RR in Nebraska from 1 Jan 1880, the leasehold passing to the Chicago, Burlington & Quincy on 26 Jul 1880 (deeded to the CB&Q 15 Feb 1908 - title only, not an operator change). Drawn here: two A&N-era features (Atchison - Salem 1871-1879, Salem - Lincoln 1872-1879) and two CB&Q-era features (Rulo - Lincoln 1880-1965 [OPEN], the 1887 Rulo bridge line 1887-1965 [OPEN]). Rule 4 split: the A&N features end 1879 and the CB&Q features start 1880 on identical geometry.

metadata.not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] ENDS: both CB&Q features (cbq-atchison-nebraska-rulo-lincoln, cbq-atchison-nebraska-rulo-bridge-line) end in 1965 because the May 1965 Burlington timetable is the last source found; it lists the Napier - Lincoln branch train (Table 63, 'consult agent', almost certainly a mixed). When that train actually stopped - before the 2 Mar 1970 BN merger, at it, or at Amtrak in 1971 - is UNKNOWN; Nebraska State Railway Commission discontinuance orders 1965-1971 are the likely source. Do not extend without evidence. 1880-1939 INTERIOR: no dated CB&Q-era passenger source between the 1875 Guide and June 1940 was found for Table Rock - Lincoln, nor for the Rulo bridge line between its 1887 construction and 1940; Rulo - Table Rock has only the 1882 Andreas anchor at Falls City. An 1880s-1920s Burlington timetable or Official Guide would settle it. ATCHISON - RULO AFTER 1879: the Kansas line's CB&Q-era passenger service is not drawn at all - no dated post-1880 passenger source was found, and its passenger end is unknown (the only data point is a c.1933 abandonment from one secondary source, a blog caption quoting a correspondent; OHM gives the grade an end_date of 1940, an unsourced conflict). Neither year is a passenger end. Next steps: a CB&Q public timetable c.1900-1932, the 1893/1910 Official Guide, or Kansas newspapers (Troy Kansas Chief, White Cloud Globe, Atchison Daily Globe). 1871 OPERATOR: no source names who ran Edwards' 1871 'regular trains' to Salem; ICC says the A&N 'probably' operated from some time in 1872. THROUGH-TRAIN REROUTING: when the Kansas City - Billings trains left Falls City for Omaha (between Sep 1951 and May 1965) is not established.
metadata.source_conflicts: Opening days differ between ICC 1917 and Edwards 1917 (Falls City 10 vs 4 Jul 1871; Table Rock 10 Nov vs 6 Dec 1871; Tecumseh 22 vs 15 Apr 1872; Lincoln 1 Sep vs 27 Aug 1872) but every year agrees. Edwards' '106.5 miles' Atchison - Lincoln is irreconcilable with ICC 144.91 mi and the timetables' ~148 mi and is treated as an error. Kansas-line length: Fowler 46.2 mi vs ICC 45.43 mi (terminal and Rulo Y differences). A 1902 map reproduced on the towns-and-nature blog labels the White Cloud line 'Missouri Pacific'; ICC 1917 is unambiguous that it was the A&N's, CB&Q-operated - the label is an error. Kansas-line abandonment: c.1933 (blog) vs OHM end_date 1940 (unsourced).
metadata.lines_not_drawn_here: Report block [6] Burlington and Missouri River in Nebraska as lessee, 1 Jan - 26 Jul 1880: not drawn (no in-era passenger evidence; at most a 1880 [ANCHOR] in the B&MR colour, which the report recommends against). Block [7] CB&Q Atchison - Rulo (Kansas line) after 1879: omitted, no confirmed CB&Q-era passenger year. Block [13] Burlington and Southwestern Rulo - near Falls City 1869-70: built but never operated by its owner (ICC p. 183); its track is drawn as part of the A&N/CB&Q features. Blocks [11] Kansas City - St. Joseph - Lincoln through trains and [12] St. Louis/KC - St. Joseph - Denver through trains ride the Rulo - Lincoln and bridge-line features and are not drawn separately; the Napier - Fortescue approach (St. Joseph & Nebraska) and the CB&Q-built Table Rock - Pawnee City - Wymore piece of [12] are outside this road and remain undrawn. Block [14] Nebraska Railway Lancaster - Lincoln (~4 mi) is drawn as the last stretch of the Salem - Lincoln and Rulo - Lincoln features (trackage), not as a separate feature.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing drawn after May 1965. Whatever freight-only years followed on the Rulo - Lincoln line (BN, then BNSF, which still runs it) are out of scope. The Kansas line is drawn only for its A&N passenger years.

segments.note: Atchison and Nebraska Railroad, report blocks [1] Atchison - Rulo (the Kansas line) and [2] Rulo - Salem. Track: Kansas line complete to the state line 11 Jan 1871 (ICC) / 10 Jan (Edwards); Falls City 10 Jul (ICC) / 4 Jul (Edwards) 1871; Rulo late July 1871 (ICC). Edwards: 'completed to Salem by the 24th of August, 1871, and the regular trains all ran west to that place and connected with the stages for Humboldt, Table Rock, Pawnee City, Beatrice and Tecumseh' - the one piece of positive 1871 passenger evidence, and the reason 1871 is drawn this far and no farther. SOURCE CONFLICT/HEDGE: ICC 1917 says there is 'nothing of record' for when the A&N began operating and that it 'probably operated the line ... from some time in 1872'; no source names the 1871 operator (the consolidated A&N existed from 10 Aug 1871, so it is the natural operator, but a contractor operation is not excluded). The ICC-safe start would be 1872. Feb 1875 Official Guide (Fowler letter y) confirms every station: Atchison, Doniphan, Brenner, Troy Junction, Fanning, Sparks, Iowa Point, White Cloud, Gibraltar, Rulo, Preston (Bluffton), Falls City, Salem. The Rulo - near-Falls-City 8 mi was built 1869-70 by the Burlington and Southwestern Ry, which never operated it (ICC p. 183), and conveyed to the A&N 1870-71. The A&N's own operation ends 31 Dec 1879: leased 999 years to the B&MR in Nebraska from 1 Jan 1880, whose leasehold passed to the CB&Q on 26 Jul 1880. Rulo - Salem continues as the CB&Q feature in this file. Atchison - Rulo is NOT drawn after 1879: passenger trains surely continued under the Burlington, but no dated post-1880 passenger source for the Kansas line was found (the line was abandoned c.1933 per one secondary source - an abandonment, not a passenger end). Headway is an estimate, NOT sourced.

segments.note: Atchison and Nebraska Railroad, report blocks [3] Salem - Table Rock, [4] Table Rock - Tecumseh and [5] Tecumseh - Lincoln, all drawable 1872-1879. Track: Dawson 8 Sep 1871 and Table Rock 10 Nov (ICC) / 6 Dec (Edwards) 1871, after which work was suspended for the winter - there is NO 1871 passenger evidence west of Salem, so 1871 is deliberately not drawn here. Tecumseh 22 Apr (ICC) / opened 15 Apr (Edwards) 1872; Sterling 5 Jun 1872; Lincoln completed 1 Sep 1872 (ICC), and per Edwards 'the first passenger train went through to the Nebraska state capitol' on 27 Aug 1872. Feb 1875 Official Guide (Fowler letter y) confirms Dawson, Humboldt, Table Rock, Elk Creek, Tecumseh, Sterling, Adams, Firth, Hickman and Saltillo. Trains ran the last ~4 mi from Lancaster into Lincoln over the Nebraska Railway (ex-Midland Pacific) by trackage. Ends 31 Dec 1879: leased to the B&MR in Nebraska 1 Jan 1880, leasehold to the CB&Q 26 Jul 1880; continues as the CB&Q feature in this file. Edwards' '106.5 miles from Atchison' to Lincoln is irreconcilable with ICC and the timetables (~148 mi) and is taken as an error in that source. Headway is an estimate, NOT sourced.

segments.note: Chicago, Burlington and Quincy over the Atchison and Nebraska, report blocks [8] Rulo - Table Rock and [9] Table Rock - Lincoln. The A&N was leased to the B&MR in Nebraska from 1 Jan 1880; the CB&Q operated as assignee of the lease from 26 Jul 1880 (ICC 1917 p. 354). The B&MR's seven lessee months are not drawn as a separate feature (report block [6]: no in-era passenger evidence; the B&MR layer's own convention), so CB&Q starts in 1880. The 15 Feb 1908 deed of the A&N to the CB&Q changed title only, not the operator, so there is no split there; the Burlington advertised the line as the 'Atchison & Nebraska Division of the B. & M.' in the 1880s (Andreas 1882), a division name only. THE 1880-1939 INTERIOR IS THINLY SOURCED: the only dated CB&Q-era passenger evidence before 1940 is Andreas (1882), whose Falls City eating house 'Has four daily passenger trains' - on Rulo - Table Rock only. On Table Rock - Lincoln the FIRST dated CB&Q-era passenger source is the June 1940 timetable; 1880-1939 there rests on interpolation between the A&N-era 1872/1875 evidence and 1940, on what was the Burlington's through Kansas City - Lincoln route (and from 1887 also the St. Louis/KC - St. Joseph - Denver route as far as Table Rock), and on Fowler's listings. A strictly confirmed-only drawing of Table Rock - Lincoln would start in 1940. No 1880s-1920s Burlington timetable or Official Guide was consulted. Headway is an estimate from Andreas' four daily trains at Falls City (two each way), NOT sourced elsewhere on the line.
sources: Segment-level: start 1880 from ICC 1917 p. 354 (lease and assignment); 1882 passenger anchor at Falls City from Andreas. NOT SOURCED AT SEGMENT LEVEL for Table Rock - Lincoln 1880-1939: no dated source between the A&N-era 1875 Guide and June 1940 was found.

segments.note: Chicago, Burlington and Quincy. DATED PASSENGER EVIDENCE: Jun 1940 Burlington timetable Table 12 (Kansas City - St. Joseph - Lincoln) prints times at Falls City, Humboldt, Table Rock, Tecumseh, Sterling, Adams, Firth, Hickman, Roca and Lincoln for through trains 41/43 and 42/44, plus a 'Daily mixed train St. Joseph to Lincoln'; its index also puts Preston, Falls City, Dawson, Humboldt and Table Rock in Table 6 (St. Louis - KC - Denver via Table Rock). Dec 1947 timetable: times at Tecumseh, Sterling, Firth; index lists Falls City, Humboldt, Dawson, Preston, Salem, Table Rock, Rulo in Tables 6/12. Sep 1951 (Feb 1952 Official Guide) Table 20 'Kansas City, St. Joseph, Lincoln and Billings' prints times at Falls City, Humboldt, Table Rock, Elk Creek, Tecumseh, St. Mary, Sterling; Table 7 lists Rulo - Table Rock stations. By May 1965 the through KC - Billings trains ran via Omaha (Table C), the change date between 1952 and 1965 not established; local service continued as the branch train of Table 63. THE 1965 END IS THE LAST CONFIRMED YEAR, NOT A KNOWN END [OPEN]. The May 1965 Burlington public timetable lists this line as Table 63 'Napier - Lincoln' under 'BRANCH LINE TRAIN SERVICE - Consult Agent for Details' (set against a separate 'FREIGHT SERVICE ONLY' column, and the station index gives no freight-only mark), so a train with passenger accommodation, almost certainly a mixed, still ran; no times are printed. No source consulted dates when that train stopped - it may have lasted to the CB&Q/BN merger (2 Mar 1970) or to Amtrak (1 May 1971), or ended sooner. The end year is a withheld unknown, not an ending. DO NOT extend this line without evidence. Headway is an estimate (several through trains plus a mixed in 1940-51; one unscheduled mixed by 1965), NOT sourced as a frequency.

THIS FEATURE was traced as a separate leg Rulo - Fortescue (5.6 mi, all on old_railway_operator=CB&Q ways, no straight legs) and cut. RULO BRIDGE LINE: live BNSF from the Rulo end of the Missouri River bridge east into Missouri, traced on old_railway_operator=CB&Q ways and cut at 3.42 mi (ICC 1917's length; 2.95 mi of it in Missouri) - the cut point is therefore measured along the trace, not located on the ground, and the documented connection with the St. Joseph & Nebraska RR is '~2.5 mi west of Fortescue'; the cut lands about 2.2 mi west of Fortescue. The feature starts about 0.3 km east of the Rulo Y point used by the main-line features. The Napier - Fortescue - junction approach is St. Joseph & Nebraska (KCStJ&CB) track and is deliberately not drawn here. Modern centreline on the 1887 bridge route; the bridge structure itself has been rebuilt since, and the drawn line follows today's.

segments.note: Chicago, Burlington and Quincy: Rulo - connection with the St. Joseph & Nebraska RR west of Fortescue, MO, across the Missouri River bridge at Rulo (report block [10]; 3.42 mi, 2.95 mi in Missouri, ICC 1917). Built 1886-1887 by the Atchison and Nebraska company but after the 1880 lease, so it was CB&Q-operated from opening and never an A&N operation. It opened the St. Joseph - Rulo - Lincoln routing used by the Kansas City - Lincoln and St. Louis/KC - Denver through trains. 1887 is a CONSTRUCTION date; the first DATED passenger evidence over the bridge is the June 1940 timetable, so 1887-1939 rests on the bridge's purpose as the through route and is not confirmed year by year (strictly confirmed-only, this line would start in 1940). Headway is an estimate, NOT sourced.

segments.note: Chicago, Burlington and Quincy. June 1940 timetable Tables 6/12 and Sep 1951 (Feb 1952 Official Guide) Table 7 'St. Louis - Kansas City - St. Joseph - Denver' (Forest City, Fortescue, Rulo ...) route trains over the bridge; May 1965 Table 63 'Napier - Lincoln' runs Napier 0 - Fortescue 4 - Rulo 10, i.e. across it. THE 1965 END IS THE LAST CONFIRMED YEAR, NOT A KNOWN END [OPEN]. The May 1965 Burlington public timetable lists this line as Table 63 'Napier - Lincoln' under 'BRANCH LINE TRAIN SERVICE - Consult Agent for Details' (set against a separate 'FREIGHT SERVICE ONLY' column, and the station index gives no freight-only mark), so a train with passenger accommodation, almost certainly a mixed, still ran; no times are printed. No source consulted dates when that train stopped - it may have lasted to the CB&Q/BN merger (2 Mar 1970) or to Amtrak (1 May 1971), or ended sooner. The end year is a withheld unknown, not an ending. DO NOT extend this line without evidence. Headway is an estimate, NOT sourced.
